deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a heavily corrected pencil draft of a letter from Riemann, signed 'B. Riemann', 'Ihr gehorsamster College'. It is addressed to a 'Verehrtester Herr Ober-Medicinal-Rath'; the original salutation 'Hochgeehrter Herr Hofrath' is struck out. From internal evidence the addressee is almost certainly the Göttingen anatomist Jakob Henle. The letter cites the addressee's 'Handbuch der systematischen Anatomie des Menschen', and Henle held the title Ober-Medicinal-Rath.

The letter runs as follows:
- Geh. Hofrath (Wilhelm) Weber has told the addressee about Riemann's investigation of the ear and obtained his promise of help.
- Riemann is almost entirely ignorant of anatomy. Even if he attended anatomy lectures and used the literature in the university library, it would be extraordinarily hard for him to find exactly the points that matter for his investigation.
- His present state of health confines him to his room, so he has had to limit himself to carefully studying the description of the ear in the Handbuch.
- The more he has worked on the subject, the more he has seen that oral instruction by an anatomist and his own inspection of the anatomy of the human ear are indispensable. The text usually says nothing explicit on his questions, and nothing certain can be read off the figures.
- He therefore asks the addressee to give him the necessary explanations orally.
- He regards the investigation of the labyrinth/inner ear as the main part of his work. At present, however, he is occupied with the mechanics of the middle ear (tympanic cavity; reading uncertain). He specifically needs to know:
  - the form of the stapes footplate;
  - the position, relative to this base, of the incudo-stapedial joint;
  - the position, relative to this base, of the insertion point of the musculus stapedius.
- On the other anatomical relations, his own inspection of preparations would be very desirable but not as indispensable as for the stapes.
- Closing formulas follow.

This is the background to Riemann's posthumously published fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres', edited by Henle in Henle & Pfeufer's Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin, 1866/67, and included in the Gesammelte Werke. No derivations are present to reconstruct.

results.what: Draft letter documenting Riemann's request to the anatomist (Henle) for anatomical instruction on the middle ear (stapes footplate, incudo-stapedial joint, insertion of m. stapedius) for his work on the mechanics of hearing
results.modern_name: Biographical/historical document; context of Riemann's 'Mechanik des Ohres' (middle-ear mechanics, ossicular chain)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's ear work is known through its posthumous publication by Henle (1866/67) and the Gesammelte Werke

deep.surprise_reason: No mathematics on the page. It is a draft cover letter, and Riemann's work on the ear and his contact with Henle via Weber are already documented by Henle's edition of 'Mechanik des Ohres'. The draft adds only minor biographical detail: his illness confining him indoors, and his specific stapes-related questions.
transcription_corrections: Addressee is evidently Henle (Ober-Medicinal-Rath, author of the 'Handbuch der systematischen Anatomie des Menschen'). The interlinear insertion 'syst.' before 'Anatomie' fits this title.
'Gegenwärtig liegt ich' should most likely read 'Gegenwärtig bin ich ... mit der Mechanik der Paukenhöhle beschäftigt'. The transcribed 'dem Mechanik' should be 'der Mechanik'.
'Untersuchung über das Labyrinth[?]': the reading of the organ named is uncertain in the image. It is in any case the inner-ear part, which Riemann calls the 'Haupttheil' of the work.
The final clause should read roughly 'welche die Form der Steigbügelplatte und die Lage, welche gegen diese Basis das Amboß-Steigbügel-Gelenk und der Insertionspunkt des m. stapedius haben'.

The passage rendered 'Ebenso ist das Wasser ... aus deutlichen ... Aufhellung der Basis stärker ist' is a struck/garbled region. 'Wasser' and 'aus deutlichen' are doubtful and may be '... anderen ... noch deutlicher'. It should be treated as illegible rather than relied upon.
Signature line 'Ihr gehorsamster College B. Riemann' is correct. 'Insertion' at the bottom left is a later or marginal note marking where the closing salutation is to be inserted.
